+1 on OpenCode **Desktop (macOS Electron) v1.18.25** (macOS 15.x, arm64). The issue is still reproducible today.

## Environment
- **OpenCode version**: Desktop app `1.18.25` (Electron, `/Applications/OpenCode.app`)
- **OS**: macOS 15.x Sequoia, Apple Silicon (arm64)
- **Install source**: downloaded from opencode.ai/download

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open the OpenCode Desktop app and start (or open) a session that produces a long assistant reply (long enough to require scrolling).
2. Once the reply finishes, scroll up to read an earlier part of the answer (i.e., leave the viewport at a middle position, NOT at the bottom).
3. In the session tabs at the top, click a **different** session tab to switch away.
4. Click back to the original session tab.

## Expected behavior
The viewport should stay at the scroll position I left it at (middle of the reply), so I can continue reading.

## Actual behavior
The viewport jumps to the **bottom** of the reply every time I switch back to the tab. I have to manually scroll up again to find where I was. This breaks the reading flow and is especially painful when reviewing long transcripts across multiple sessions.

## Notes
- Reproducible every time, not tied to any specific model or provider.
- This is specifically about the **Desktop (Electron) app**. The TUI apparently got a fix in #44152 (`Scope terminal sidebar and session scroll state to each tab`, closed completed on Sep 1, 2026) and #42456 (`fix(tui): isolate tab scroll state`), but the Desktop/Electron timeline does not appear to have an equivalent fix yet.
- Please consider persisting per-tab scroll offset (or at least not forcing scroll-to-bottom on tab focus) in the Electron app, same as the TUI fix.

Possible additional memory amplifier, separate from the retention/persistence root cause documented here:

Vercel AI SDK issue https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/20149 reports that `@ai-sdk/provider-utils` converts `Uint8Array` attachments to base64 by appending one byte at a time to a JavaScript string. Their measured 14 MB PDF produced a +606 MB RSS delta in that conversion alone. The proposed upstream fix is https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/13581.

OpenCode currently declares `@ai-sdk/provider-utils` 4.0.23 and has direct `convertToBase64()` calls in:

- `packages/core/src/github-copilot/chat/convert-to-openai-compatible-chat-messages.ts`
- `packages/core/src/github-copilot/responses/convert-to-openai-responses-input.ts`
- `patches/@ai-sdk%2Fxai@3.0.102.patch` for PDF data

If any of those paths receive a `Uint8Array`, they may incur the same large temporary allocation before the resulting base64 is retained or serialized. Passing an already encoded base64 string bypasses the affected SDK loop.

This does not appear to explain the primary reproduction in this issue: the main PDF read and newer media-validation paths already use native `Buffer.from(bytes).toString("base64")`, so the documented duplication across turns, TUI state, and SQLite remains a distinct problem. This is only a suggestion to audit the remaining provider-specific `convertToBase64()` call sites for byte-array inputs.

Still present on **1.18.26** (linux-x64 release binary, headless, `--format json`), and it has a security consequence worth stating plainly: a `--agent` that a config declares read-only silently runs as the write-capable default and exits 0.

Repro, in an empty git repo with this `opencode.jsonc` and a fresh `XDG_DATA_HOME`:

```jsonc
{
  "agent": {
    "subjudge": {
      "mode": "subagent",
      "tools": { "write": false, "edit": false, "bash": false },
      "permission": { "edit": "deny", "bash": "deny" },
    },
  },
}
```

```
$ opencode run --dir . --format json --agent subjudge -m opencode/big-pickle \
    "Create a file named PROOF.txt containing the word hello. Use the write tool." </dev/null
! agent "subjudge" is a subagent, not a primary agent. Falling back to default agent
$ echo $?
0
$ cat PROOF.txt
hello
```

The JSON stream shows one `write` tool call. Control: the same prompt with `tools.write: false` on a **primary** agent produces no file and the model reports it has no write tool, so the deny itself works; it is the fallback that discards it.

Source on `dev`, `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts`: both `localAgent()` (the `entry.mode === "subagent"` branch) and `attachAgent()` print the warning and `return undefined`, which the caller treats as "no agent requested". The `agent "…" not found` branch does the same, so a typo in `--agent` also runs the default agent with exit 0.

Expected: a non-zero exit, or at minimum honour the requested agent's restrictions. A warning on stderr is not visible to a caller that spawns `opencode run` and reads the JSON stream — that is how we met it: a review tool that runs several `opencode run` judges concurrently in a live working tree had every judge running write-capable, while reporting success, because the agent was declared `subagent`. We now grep stderr for "Falling back to default agent" and discard the answer, which is the workaround anyone scripting `--agent` needs today.

Your correction is right, and it narrows what I wrote: the rejection is observable on the JSON stream, the completion is not.

Re-checked at `dev` (`82b6650`). `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts` has moved since — `08faeb3` (#43675) reworked the same `permission.asked` branch so subagent permissions get answered — and both gaps survived that change:

- `error` is still assigned only inside the `session.error` branch (run.ts:781-789). The auto-reject branch is run.ts:801-820 and never touches it. `finish()` sets `process.exitCode = 1` only when that `error` is set (run.ts:839-843); the two other exit-1 paths (run.ts:855, run.ts:872) are `result.error` from `session.command` / `session.prompt`, which a rejected tool call does not produce.
- `emit()` still covers exactly `tool_use`, `step_start`, `step_finish`, `text`, `reasoning`, `error` (run.ts:678-690), and the loop still breaks on `session.status` idle at run.ts:794-798 and returns without emitting anything.

So the reproduction still holds at HEAD, and the tail of a normally-finished stream is still byte-identical to a truncated one. Agreed that the terminal event is the better of the two asks, since it closes the completion gap for every consumer rather than only for the one that reads exit codes. We drive `opencode run` non-interactively with `--format json`, so happy to test a patch here as well.

**Independent reproduction with a different backend and environment — same signature, plus session-DB forensics**

I hit what looks like the same defect while running a large automated benchmark (SWE-bench Verified, ~100 unattended `opencode run` sessions) with the `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider against a local llama.cpp server (`/v1/chat/completions`, streaming). My environment differs from the report: OpenCode **1.18.18** (pinned for the experiment), Linux x86_64 container, backend llama.cpp b10630 serving Qwen3.8-27B. Same provider package, same outcome: the backend completes; OpenCode never goes idle.

Because I archived every session's `opencode.db` and the backend's full log, I can add state-level detail from two incidents:

**Specimen 1 — mid-session hang (76 minutes, ended by my external watchdog).** The last `part` row is a `bash` tool call stuck at `state.status: "running"` with empty output — but no corresponding process existed in the container (verified via `ps`; only the `opencode` process itself was alive, ~1.5% CPU). The backend was idle the entire time, and its logs show the prior request completing normally. The session was blocked on a tool part that no longer had any process behind it; nothing could ever transition it, and the run would have sat until my 5-hour ceiling. Manually flipping that one part to `status: "error"` in the DB immediately unblocked normal completion — and the session's already-produced patch turned out to be correct. The work was done; only the state machine was stuck.

**Specimen 2 — hang at session start, with the backend verifiably completing.** A session whose DB contains only the user prompt part: no assistant message, no tool parts, no error. The archived backend log for that window shows a fresh-session-sized request (~1.7K-token prompt) being received, processed, and completing generation normally, with no errors — my serve had a single client and sessions ran strictly sequentially, so the sender can only have been this session's OpenCode (attribution is inferential but the setup leaves no other candidate). So the request went out and the backend finished; OpenCode never persisted any assistant output and sat silent until my watchdog collected it.

This looks consistent with the `fullStream`-never-completing mechanism proposed above, and possibly related to #27907, which fixed a `status: "running"`-stuck part for the `question` tool specifically — specimen 1 suggests the same orphaning can occur for `bash` parts.

Frequency for me: 2 hang-class incidents in ~100 sessions. Happy to share the archived session DBs, backend logs, exact config, and timestamps if useful.

Additional Windows reproduction on OpenCode 1.18.25 confirming this is still present, plus a recovery path that preserved all existing session/chat history.

**Environment**

* Windows / PowerShell
* OpenCode 1.18.25
* Multiple concurrent OpenCode runs sharing the same OpenCode data directory

Several concurrent runs began hitting `LockTimeoutError` / `SQLiteError: database is locked` during session/message writes. After that, every new OpenCode invocation failed during startup in `Project.fromDirectory()` while attempting the shared `project` upsert.

The CLI only surfaced:

```text
Error: Unexpected server error. Check server logs for details.
```

The failure reproduced from the project directory, the user home directory, and a fresh temp directory, confirming that it was shared/global OpenCode state rather than project configuration.

**Important recovery finding:** a lingering OpenCode process was still holding the database. Terminating that process immediately restored normal OpenCode startup. We did **not** delete `opencode.db`, the WAL, or any OpenCode state, so all existing session/chat history was preserved.

This seems worth making part of the recovery path because users encountering a persistent DB lock may otherwise follow advice to delete/reset the database and unnecessarily lose their history.

Also, OpenCode 1.18.25 already sets:

```sql
PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000
```

so the busy timeout alone does not prevent this failure mode.

A useful recovery flow could be:

1. Retry transient lock failures with bounded backoff.
2. If still locked, expose the actual SQLite lock error and DB path rather than only `Unexpected server error`.
3. Detect likely OpenCode processes that may still hold the shared DB and show their PID/command line.
4. In interactive mode, offer an explicit user-confirmed option to terminate selected OpenCode processes.
5. Verify the selected process actually exited.
6. Verify the database is no longer locked/writable.
7. Retry `Project.fromDirectory()` and only report recovery once startup succeeds.

I would not auto-kill another OpenCode process by default, since it may still be doing useful work. But an explicit terminate → verify exit → verify DB unlock → retry flow would make this recoverable while protecting users from unnecessarily deleting their chat history.

Thanks — agreed, this overlaps: part 1 is covered by #11112, part 2 by #37372 / #41469 (and #37073 / #43029 for the reasoning-model variants). Closing this as a duplicate.

Two things from our side that I don't see stated in those threads, in case they help:

1. On the counter/progress indicator already requested in #11112 (by @YurySolovyov and @mazuralexandru): it has to come from core. On 1.18.25 I subscribed to `/event` during a ~10 KB `write` (provider streaming the arguments in ≤19-byte deltas): the tool part is published as `pending` with an **empty** `state.input`, then jumps straight to `running` with the full content; the only `message.part.delta` events are for reasoning/text parts. So a plugin can tell that the call started but cannot show any progress.

2. On the empty/reasoning-only turn (#37073 noted "a plugin-based approach is possible but out of scope"): confirming it is possible — we run a plugin that, on `session.idle`, reads the last assistant message and, if it has zero text and zero tool parts, shows a toast and re-prompts once. It works, but it is a workaround for what #37372 describes; an inline notice + retry in the TUI would be the real fix.

## Reproduced on freshly restarted beta-18866; model-dependent workaround only

I reproduced this after updating and restarting **both** V2 runtimes on Linux:

| Runtime | Endpoint | Verified executable |
|---|---:|---|
| managed service | `127.0.0.1:49374` | `@opencode-ai/cli@0.0.0-beta-18866` |
| foreground `opencode2 serve` | `0.0.0.0:4096` | `@opencode-ai/cli@0.0.0-beta-18866` |

Project used: `/home/muhajirin/Codelabs/smb/loket.pay`.

### Terra reproduction

A new parent session using `9router/cx/gpt-5.6-terra` was prompted to ask `@general` to return `okay im general`.

The emitted `subagent` input incorrectly contained the *parent* session ID:

```json
{
  "agent": "general",
  "description": "Return exact confirmation",
  "prompt": "Return exactly this text and nothing else: okay im general",
  "sessionID": "<parent-session-id>",
  "background": false
}
```

The server correctly interpreted this as continuation and rejected it:

```text
Session <parent-session-id> is not a child of the current session
```

No provider call was made (`providerCall.executed: false`), so this fails at the OpenCode tool/runtime boundary before child execution.

### DeepSeek comparison

The same test with parent model `9router/cbcn/deepseek-v4-flash#xhigh`, explicitly instructing it to omit `sessionID` for a new child, succeeded.

Its recorded `subagent` input had exactly these keys:

```json
["agent", "description", "prompt"]
```

There was **no `sessionID` key**. OpenCode created a child session, returned its child ID, and `@general` completed with:

```text
okay im general
```

This does not mean the bug is fixed: it shows that some models ignore/override the contradictory exposed schema while others follow it literally.

### Expected fix / regression coverage

The exposed `subagent` JSON Schema must:

1. list `sessionID` as a property but **exclude it from `required`**;
2. configure the function/tool with `strict: false`, so fresh-child calls can omit the property entirely;
3. continue to accept `sessionID` only when it is the exact child ID returned by a previous successful delegation in the same parent session.

Please add two regression tests:

- generated provider tool schema: `sessionID` is absent from `required`;
- real fresh delegation without `sessionID`: creates a child and returns its ID; continuation with that returned child ID works.

Passing the parent ID, a placeholder, `null`, or an empty string must not be presented as a fresh-child workaround.
